title: Segoe UI typeface
lede: The humanist sans-serif that actually set the text of Vista and Windows 7, and the typeface behind the “Frutiger” in the name.
summary: Rounded humanist sans-serif of the Aero interfaces. Monotype for Microsoft, first shipped with Windows Vista.
made: Segoe designed c. 2000 at Agfa Monotype; Segoe UI first introduced with Windows Vista

evidence.note: Inspected [File:Segoe UI Revision Differences.png](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Segoe_UI_Revision_Differences.png) (1200 × 650, PD-font) and stored it. Also saw Segoe UI in the Vista and Windows 7 screenshots inspected for [Windows Vista](ref:windows-vista-aero-interface) and [Windows 7](ref:windows-7-aero-interface).

styles.note: Segoe UI is the humanist interface type of Windows Aero, and CARI links it to Frutiger in the style’s name.

context: Segoe was designed by Steve Matteson at Agfa Monotype and licensed to Microsoft. Segoe UI “was first introduced with Windows Vista” and replaced Tahoma as the interface font; Light and Semibold weights came with Windows 7. [Wikipedia: Segoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segoe).

In 2004 Linotype protested Microsoft’s EU design registration of Segoe, citing its similarity to Frutiger; the EU revoked the registration. Microsoft states that Segoe was not derived from Frutiger. [Wikipedia: Segoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segoe).
CARI says Frutiger “originally inspired Vista’s default font (Segoe UI).” [CARI: Frutiger Aero](https://cari.institute/aesthetics/frutiger-aero). This is CARI’s claim; Microsoft disputes derivation.
In October 2011 the letters I and Q and several figures were redrawn; I, Q, and 1 became closer to Frutiger. [Wikipedia: Segoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segoe).
observed: The top line (Vista and Windows 7 version) shows “IQ124578” with round, open forms; the I has serifs, the 1 has a foot, and the Q tail sweeps down and out to the right.
The bottom line (2011 revision) has a plain I, a 1 without a foot, and a short straight Q tail; the 2, 4, 5, 7, and 8 are also redrawn.
In the Vista and Windows 7 screenshots, menu and window text is set in small, even, humanist sans-serif.
interpretation: If a catalogue specimen needs “the” Frutiger Aero typeface, Segoe UI is the documented interface face; Frutiger names the tradition. Both are humanist and open.
borrow: Use Segoe UI (or a free humanist substitute) at small, regular weights for body and control labels; keep headings light rather than heavy.

images.alt: Two lines of black text reading IQ124578. The upper line is Segoe UI from Windows Vista and Windows 7; the lower line is the 2011 revision with different I, Q, 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, and 8.
images.caption: Segoe UI before (top, Vista and Windows 7) and after (bottom) the 2011 revision. [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Segoe_UI_Revision_Differences.png), tagged PD-font.
